jobs.description: Employer: Community Health and Counseling Services Expires: 09/23/2026 e are proud to announce the launch of the new Crisis Receiving Center located in Penobscot County—a safe, compassionate, and accessible place for individuals experiencing a behavioral health crisis.The Center is designed to reduce unnecessary emergency department visits and keep people out of the criminal justice system by providing immediate assessment, triage, and support in a calm, therapeutic environment. The Peer Specialist works as a member of a team of professionals who provide treatment and services to people who utilize the crisis receiving center to access mental health and co-occurring substance abuse services. The Peer Specialist contributes to the Agency’s mission to assist individuals with recovery from psychiatric and substance use difficulties through the provision of a wide range of non-clinical activities that engage, educate, and support individuals, their family members and caregivers. The Peer Specialist provides recovery training and outreach to peers in both group and individual settings while demonstrating the values of hopefulness for recovery, respect, acceptance, personal responsibility, honesty, and self-advocacy to both peers and colleagues. For the purposes of this job description peer is defined as an individual who has lived experience. Must have a high school diploma/GED or higher education; must have personally experienced mental Illness or substance use disorder. Must have Certified Intentional Peer Support Specialist (CIPPS) Certification or be willing to obtain certification within the first 9 months of employment. Must attend Peer Support 101 prior to practicing peer support with clients at the center. Must apply for the next available Core Training within 30 days of employment. Prior experience working in a mental health setting is a plus. jobs.title: Residential Counselor at Stability Mental Health
jobs.description: Employer: Stability Mental Health Expires: 09/23/2026 Job detailsHere’s how the job details align with your profile.Pay Full job descriptionAbout SMH AcademySMH Academy is a residential mental health program serving young adults ages 18–26. The program uses a whole-person model of care — addressing environment, nutrition, exercise, sleep, hygiene, community, and talk therapy alongside medication management when clinically indicated. Behavioral support is built on an earned-incentive framework rather than punitive discipline, and all programming is neurodiversity-affirming.Position OverviewThe Residential Counselor is a direct-support, mentorship-style role — not a clinical position. No degree or prior mental health experience is required, but it is preferred. Comprehensive paid training is provided, including instruction in neurodiversity-affirming care, the program's behavioral framework, and de-escalation techniques.Residential Counselors work on-site with residents day to day, helping them stay on schedule, stay positive, and build the practical skills needed for independent living. A licensed therapist is on-site three days per week; Residential Counselors coordinate with the clinical team but do not provide therapy themselves.What You'll DoHold the schedule: Help residents follow the house's daily schedule, including meals, activities, and structured routines.Guide and redirect: Model a positive, encouraging attitude and respond to setbacks with patience and calm redirection.Teach life skills: Teach and support daily living skills — laundry, cooking, grocery shopping, budgeting, and household upkeep.Support neurodiversity-affirming care: Recognize and respond supportively to each resident's individual needs, communication style, and sensory preferences.Document and communicate: Note resident mood, participation, and any concerns each shift, and pass along updates to incoming staff and the clinical team.Maintain the household environment: Maintain a respectful, safe, and encouraging home environment at all times.What We're Looking ForMinimum High School Diploma — this role is fully trained on the job.A genuine interest in mental health, neurodiversity, and helping young adults build independence.Patience, reliability, and a calm, positive presence, including during difficult moments.Strong communication skills and comfort working as part of a team.Ability to pass a background check.Minimum age of 19 yearsValid driver's licenseCPR/First Aid certification (can be completed during training)Training & SupportAll Residential Counselors complete paid training before working independently with residents, covering the program's behavioral framework, neurodiversity-affirming care practices, de-escalation and redirection techniques, and house procedures. Ongoing supervision and support are provided by the clinical and program leadership team.Schedule & Compensation8 or 12 hours shifts available, flexible schedule as this is a 24/7 role divided between several coaches $18/hour depending on experienceTo ApplySend resume to hello@smhacademy.comPay: $18.00 per hourWork Location: In person

jobs.description: Employer: Colorado College Expires: 09/23/2026 Early Childhood Teacher (T-2)To apply, please visit: https://apptrkr.com/7263316Job Title: Early Childhood Teacher (T-2)Department: Children's CenterCampus Location: Main CampusFLSA Status: Nonexempt/ HourlyPosition Type/ Work Schedule• 2080 Hours per year• 12 Months per year• 40 Hours per week (Estimated)About UsSet at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, Colorado College is a place where individuals are determined to positively impact the world. The college actively promotes a dynamic and inclusive environment where students and employees of diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives can learn and work together. Here, you are welcomed as a valued member of the community. Colorado College is a place to explore, grow, and thrive.Job SummaryWe are seeking an Early Childhood Teacher dedicated to creating a safe, healthy, and nurturing environment for young learners and their families. In this role, you will design and implement developmentally appropriate learning experiences that support the holistic growth of each child, guided by observation and assessment. Collaboration and flexibility are key, as you will work closely with colleagues and adapt to varying classroom needs. Compliance with Colorado Department of Human Services and Health Department licensing standards is essential. jobs.title: Afterschool Site Director at Immigrant Social Services
jobs.description: Employer: Immigrant Social Services Expires: 09/24/2026 2026-2027 AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAMS SITE DIRECTORImmigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) seeks a dynamic and experienced part-time Afterschool Programs Site Director. The Site Director is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the day-to-day operations of the afterschool program site (with 35-80 enrolled students) including coaching and working with a small team of Group Leader(s)/Group Assistant (s) and volunteers/interns to create a safe, caring and enriching environment for all children at all times. The Site Director is responsible for ensuring that policies and licensing standards are met in regards to day-to day operations including maintaining up to date records, ensuring supervision policies are implemented, guiding the behavior of children, planning and delivering the weekly curriculum and managing staff. About ISS Afterschool ProgramsServing students in Pre-K through Grade 5, Immigrant Social Services (ISS) operates afterschool programs at public school sites throughout Manhattan’s Lower East Side and Chinatown. We see the out-of-school time space as an opportunity to reimagine learning, achievement, and youth development in ways that respond to the lived realities, strengths, and aspirations of immigrant students and their families.Social-emotional learning (SEL) forms the core of our afterschool programs. Through evidence-based SEL experiences, students develop the skills and mindsets they need to navigate relationships, manage emotions, solve problems, make responsible decisions, and build confidence and resilience. Whether helping a student work through a challenging homework problem, facilitating a cooperative game, or supporting a child through a difficult moment, every interaction is an opportunity to strengthen social-emotional skills and promote healthy development.Our work is grounded in Positive Youth Development (PYD), which recognizes young people as capable, resourceful individuals with strengths, ideas, and contributions to make. We create environments where students can build meaningful relationships with adults and peers, develop a sense of belonging, exercise agency, explore their interests, and experience success. Rather than focusing only on what young people need to overcome, our programs intentionally cultivate the protective factors, relationships, and opportunities that help children thrive.Within this SEL and Positive Youth Development framework, group leaders facilitate homework support, enrichment, recreation, and hands-on learning experiences that promote academic success and whole-child development. Program activities and curricular content integrate language arts and literacy, STEM, the arts, health and fitness, and social and emotional development—while creating space for curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, and compassion. Roles & Responsibilities:Manage and supervise daily onsite program operations and implementation of quality learning experiences such as:Staff Supervision and DevelopmentCoach, guide and manage the day-to-day duties of group leaders/assistants/volunteers/interns. Provide overall support and supervision for site staff, coordinate and facilitate check-ins, observations, and evaluations.Oversee and assign responsibilities each day including leading activities, helping with snack, homework support, restroom supervision, and clean up as required. Uphold ISS standards of professional practice, such as punctuality, presence and attentiveness with youth, and conduct that models what the program expects of its participants, and build a site culture where these are the norms rather than the correction. Prevent and address any staff performance concerns before they affect program quality.Provide specific input/feedback for group leaders/assistants for performance reviews.Program Quality and Youth Development Work closely with youth development professionals to implement a weekly social-emotional curriculum.Use positive group management techniques. Anticipate and deal with behavior problems proactively.Health, Safety, and Regulatory ComplianceEnsure the safety of all children enrolled in the program by following the supervision standards in NYS OCFS SACC, DOHMH, DOE, and other regulatory agencies,Maintain constant head counts when transitioning between different areas and activities. Ensure that only the authorized parent/guardian or emergency contact signs a child in/out of the program and include recording time. Return rosters to office administration weekly, signed and dated.Follow protocols for dealing with First-Aid and emergency situations. Complete necessary paperwork such as incident reports, medical log, etc.Maintain a clean and sanitary program environment by ensuring supplies, equipment and tables are cleaned before and after snack or activities. Ensure children wash their hands before snack. Report any maintenance issues to the school custodians and the Site Director.Lead monthly fire safety drill and log results to meet licensing requirements.Complete all required trainings for compliance with DOHMH, OCFS, and OASAS. Attend all staff meetings as required.Assist with planning and implementation of special events.Enrollment and Family EngagementPromote ISS programs to prospective families and support recruitment efforts to reach enrollment targets, including orientation sessions and outreach at school sites. Manage the registration process end to end: distribute and collect registration forms, verify that required documentation and information is complete, and maintain accurate, current family records. Track enrollment and registration status. Serve as the primary onsite point of contact for families, including communicating program schedules, closures, and policies; respond to questions and concerns from families and the school administration promptly.Attendance, Records, and ReportingMaintain complete and thorough attendance of all students and staff each day. Check the school absentee list, site voicemail, and call parents if child(ren) are absent, but scheduled. Submit attendance rosters, schedule changes, licensing paperwork, timesheets and other reports accurately and on time, meeting all internal and regulatory deadlines. Qualifications and Skills:Bachelor’s Degree in education or related fields, or equivalent work experience.Minimum of three years of relevant experience with elementary or middle school-age children in an afterschool program leading activities in a group setting.At least two years of supervisory experience.Experience adhering to licensing requirements. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to communicate with all levels including staff, parents/families, and school staff. Ability to problem solve and make decisions that adhere to the purpose, mission and goals of ISS.A self-starter with strong organizational, problem-solving, conflict resolution, and crisis management skills, capable of prioritizing and performing multiple tasks effectively in a fast-paced environment.Knowledge and sensitivity to the diverse perspectives inherent in working with Asian Americans/immigrants, communities of color, and low-income families.Working knowledge of the DOE/public school system, out-of-school time programs and networks, nonprofit organizations, curriculum design and implementation, program evaluation and assessment, Asian American studies, and community development is helpful.Familiarity with program outreach and marketing, a plus.Conditions of EmploymentAll candidates must complete background clearance as required by NYS OCFS and the NYC DOHMH, including State Central Register (SCR) and fingerprint-based criminal history checks, and provide proof of a Mantoux (TB) test within two weeks of hire. Employment is contingent upon satisfactory completion of these requirements and on maintaining all certifications required for the position.Compensation:This is a part-time position for the 2026-27 school year that follows the NYC DOE academic calendar. Must be available during afterschool hours, Monday–Friday, 1:00-6:00/6:30 pmPayrate: $23-$25 per hour, depending on education and experienceApplication Process:To apply, please send a cover letter and resume to hr@issnyc.org with the subject heading: "Afterschool Programs Site Director".About ISS:Founded in 1972, Immigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the conditions of underserved immigrants in Chinatown/Lower East Side, New York City. The majority of the immigrant families we serve are from low-income, monolingual Chinese-speaking multigenerational households. Through programs and services centered on care, education, prevention, and community, we nurture and empower immigrant children/youth, young adults, seniors, and families to develop and restore their agency to strengthen the wellbeing of their communities. For more information, visit www.issnyc.org. Equal Opportunity Employment:Immigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

jobs.title: Afterschool Group Leader at Immigrant Social Services
jobs.description: Employer: Immigrant Social Services Expires: 09/24/2026 2026–2027 Afterschool Programs Group LeaderPosition SummaryImmigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is seeking enthusiastic, dependable, and compassionate individuals who are passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of children and families. Group Leaders play an important role in creating safe, engaging, and inclusive afterschool environments where students can learn, build confidence, develop meaningful relationships, and discover their strengths.Serving students in Pre-K through Grade 5, Group Leaders facilitate homework support, enrichment activities, recreation, and evidence-based social-emotional learning experiences that promote academic success and healthy youth development. Every interaction—from helping a student solve a challenging homework problem to leading a cooperative game or supporting a child through a difficult moment—is an opportunity to foster resilience, confidence, and lifelong skills.Group Leaders receive comprehensive training and ongoing coaching to facilitate evidence-based curricula that strengthen students' social-emotional competencies, build protective factors, and promote healthy decision-making. Group Leaders are more than activity leaders—they are mentors, educators, and trusted adults who help children develop the skills they need to thrive both in and beyond the classroom.About ISS Afterschool ProgramsServing students in Pre-K through Grade 5, Immigrant Social Services (ISS) operates afterschool programs at public school sites throughout Manhattan’s Lower East Side and Chinatown. We see the out-of-school time space as an opportunity to reimagine learning, achievement, and youth development in ways that respond to the lived realities, strengths, and aspirations of immigrant students and their families.Social-emotional learning (SEL) forms the core of our afterschool programs. Through evidence-based SEL experiences, students develop the skills and mindsets they need to navigate relationships, manage emotions, solve problems, make responsible decisions, and build confidence and resilience. Whether helping a student work through a challenging homework problem, facilitating a cooperative game, or supporting a child through a difficult moment, every interaction is an opportunity to strengthen social-emotional skills and promote healthy development.Our work is grounded in Positive Youth Development (PYD), which recognizes young people as capable, resourceful individuals with strengths, ideas, and contributions to make. We create environments where students can build meaningful relationships with adults and peers, develop a sense of belonging, exercise agency, explore their interests, and experience success. Rather than focusing only on what young people need to overcome, our programs intentionally cultivate the protective factors, relationships, and opportunities that help children thrive.Within this SEL and Positive Youth Development framework, group leaders facilitate homework support, enrichment, recreation, and hands-on learning experiences that promote academic success and whole-child development. Program activities and curricular content integrate language arts and literacy, STEM, social studies, the arts, health and fitness, and social and emotional development—while creating space for curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, and compassion.Core ResponsibilitiesCreate Safe, Inclusive, and Supportive Learning EnvironmentsGroup Leaders help create spaces where every child feels physically and emotionally safe, welcomed, and valued.Responsibilities include:Supervise students and ensure their safety and wellbeing throughout all afterschool activities.Foster a welcoming, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed environment where children feel respected, included, and encouraged to participate.Build caring, supportive relationships that promote trust, belonging, and positive youth development.Encourage cooperation, responsibility, and respect through positive behavior support,and developmentally appropriate classroom management.Model professionalism, empathy, patience, and positive communication in all interactions with students, families, school staff, and colleagues.Recognize and respond appropriately to students' individual developmental, social emotional, and behavioral needs.Support Students Throughout the Afterschool ExperienceEvery afternoon is different. Group Leaders help create a smooth, engaging, and supportive afterschool experience by confidently guiding groups of students through a variety of activities, settings, and learning experiences. Success in this role requires flexibility, sound judgment, and the ability to adapt to students' changing needs throughout the day.Group Leaders are responsible for:Guiding students through the many parts of the afterschool day, including arrival, snack, homework, enrichment, recreation, and dismissal.Supervising students in a variety of settings, including classrooms, cafeterias, gymnasiums, playgrounds, hallways, and other shared spaces.Leading safe, organized, and positive transitions between activities while maintaining student engagement and appropriate behavior.Providing academic support and facilitating homework support in both small- and large-group settings.Recognizing when students need additional encouragement, redirection, or emotional support and responding with patience, empathy, and professionalism.Creating opportunities throughout the afternoon for students to practice leadership, cooperation, communication, and responsible decision-making.Facilitate Social-Emotional Learning ISS believes children develop important life skills through meaningful relationships, engaging learning experiences, and opportunities to practice positive behaviors every day. Group Leaders play an active role in helping students build the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to succeed in school and life.After completing ISS training and receiving ongoing coaching, Group Leaders facilitate evidence-based Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) curricula while reinforcing these skills throughout daily interactions, activities, and routines.Group Leaders help students develop:Self-awareness and self-confidenceSelf-management and emotional regulationResponsible decision-makingPositive relationship skillsSocial awareness and empathyCommunication and conflict resolution skillsProblem-solving and critical thinkingLeadership, teamwork, and cooperationBy integrating these skills into homework support, enrichment activities, recreation, and everyday interactions, Group Leaders help children build habits that contribute to long-term academic success and healthy development.Collaboration & Professional ResponsibilitiesHigh-quality afterschool programs are built through teamwork, communication, and a shared commitment to helping children succeed. Group Leaders work closely with Site Directors, fellow staff, school personnel, and families to provide a consistent, supportive experience for every student.Responsibilities include:Collaborate with Site Directors, school staff, and fellow Group Leaders to provide engaging, high-quality programming.Communicate professionally with colleagues, families, and school personnel to support student success and well-being.Promptly report concerns related to student safety, attendance, behavior, or well-being to supervisory staff.Participate actively in staff meetings, trainings, coaching sessions, and professional development opportunities.Maintain accurate attendance, lesson implementation records, and other required program documentation.Carry out responsibilities in accordance with ISS's mission, positive youth development philosophy, and organizational values.QualificationsWe're looking for individuals who enjoy working with children, are eager to learn, and are excited to make a positive impact in their community.Required QualificationsCurrently enrolled in college or have completed some college coursework.At least 18 years of age.Experience working with children in schools, afterschool programs, camps, tutoring programs, childcare settings, or other youth-serving organizations.Experience leading activities or facilitating groups of children.Ability to work during afterschool hours throughout the school year.Strong communication and interpersonal skills.Dependable, professional, and committed to creating a positive experience for children.Preferred QualificationsAbility to build supportive relationships with children and families from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds.Effective classroom management and positive behavior support skills.Strong situational judgment and adaptability, with the ability to recognize what each moment calls for—whether supporting an individual student, guiding a small group, managing transitions, or leading engaging activities for a larger group.Comfortable working in an active, fast-paced environment where schedules, settings, and student needs change throughout the afternoon.Willingness to receive coaching and implement evidence-based curricula with fidelity.Commitment to continuous professional growth and reflective practice.Bilingual in Mandarin, Cantonese, Fujianese, or Spanish preferred.Experience working with immigrant, multilingual, and underserved communities is highly desirable.Why Join ISS?At ISS, you'll do more than supervise children after school—you'll become part of a mission-driven organization dedicated to strengthening immigrant communities through education, prevention, and youth development.As an ISS Group Leader, you'll gain valuable professional experience while making a lasting impact on the lives of children and families. Whether you're pursuing a career in education, psychology, counseling, social work, public health, or another care profession, this position provides meaningful opportunities to develop practical skills that will support your future career.What You'll GainHands-on experience working with elementary-aged children in a school-based setting.Paid training in evidence-based Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) curricula.Coaching from experienced youth development professionals.Experience facilitating engaging lessons, enrichment activities, and group discussions.Leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills that transfer across education and human services careers.Experience working with culturally and linguistically diverse children and families.Opportunities to build your resume while making a meaningful difference in your community.At ISS, we believe investing in our staff is essential to providing high-quality programs for children. We are committed to supporting your growth as a youth development professional through training, mentorship, and continuous learning.Hours and Commitment: This is a part-time/contract position for the 2026-27 school year that follows the NYC DOE academic calendar. Must be available during afterschool hours, Monday–Friday, 2:00 pm/2:30 pm – 5:45 pm/6:00 pm (start and end times depend on location). Flexible days, but five days a week is preferred. Hiring is contingent upon passing a background check. Must be available for orientation in late August or early September 2026. Location: Our afterschool programs operate at public school sites in the Lower East Side/Chinatown neighborhood.Payrate: $17.00 - $18.00 per hour - depending on experienceApplication Process:To apply, please email your resume and cover letter to hr@issnyc.org with the subject line: Afterschool Programs Group Leader. About ISSFounded in 1972, Immigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the conditions of underserved immigrants in Chinatown/Lower East Side, New York City. The majority of immigrant families we serve are from low-income, monolingual Chinese-speaking multigenerational households. Through programs and services centered on care, education, prevention, and community, we nurture and empower immigrant children/youth, young adults, seniors, and families to develop and restore their agency to strengthen the wellbeing of their communities. For more information, visit www.issnyc.org. Equal Opportunity EmploymentImmigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

When completing the form, be sure to explain in detail how your qualifications are equivalent to the required minimum qualifications. Do not assume that you do not need to submit a Supplemental Questionnaire for Equivalency because your degree is similar to a degree stated in the minimum qualifications. Degree titles that are not an exact match will not be considered outside of the equivalency process.The equivalency review is an independent process for district wide disciplines that is separate from the recruitment process to fill a vacancy. A subcommittee of discipline experts that is coordinated by an Academic Senate President will review the equivalency materials and make a recommendation as to whether or not the applicant demonstrated they have qualifications that are equivalent to those shown in the minimum qualifications section of the job posting. For disciplines that are unique to a specific campus the equivalency may be done by the hiring committee along with an Academic Senate President. You will be evaluated based upon the information provided.APPLICATION PROCEDUREIf you need assistance using the online application system please contact the GovernmentJobs.com applicant support line at (855) 524-5627 between the hours of 6 AM to 5 PM, Pacific Time, Monday through Friday.All applicants, including previous and current VCCCD employees, must submit the following documents with their application in order to be considered. A completed Ventura County Community College District/GovernmentJobs.com Employment Application.All sections of the application must be filled out. Cover Letter.The cover letter of must include the following: A) the date, your name, and the position and locations for which you are applying, B) address your sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, social, economic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, and C) provide the screening committee with an understanding of how you will contribute as a fully participating member of the VCCCD community.3. Complete official or unofficial college/university transcriptsTranscripts must show the degree title and the date the degree was conferred, or the degree will not be considered for the purpose of determining if you meet minimum qualifications. jobs.description: Employer: Alpaca Health Expires: 09/24/2026 Alpaca HealthWork Location: In Person If you want work that challenges you, changes lives, and builds a real career, this is it. For many of our roles you don’t need your RBT certification to apply. What matters most is that you love working with kids, you’re dependable, and you’re ready to show up. Some roles do require an active certification, but if you’re not certified yet, we’ll help you find your path to getting there.Alpaca Health is a multi-state network of independent ABA therapists, working in homes, schools, and daycares. We hire certified RBTs and motivated people ready to become one. Either way, you’ll work alongside a dedicated BCBA who mentors you from day one, not a manager, not a corporate supervisor. Two ways to joinAlready an RBTActive RBT certificationStart working and earning right awayWork with clients in your regionA path toward BCBA if you want itNot certified yetA clear path to becoming an RBT, with a BCBA mentor from day oneMany practices in our network reimburse RBT training and pay you during hands-on learning, and we’ll help match you with the right fitSupport as you prepare for and sit for your certification exam The jobYou’ll work one-on-one with kids with autism in their homes, classrooms, and communities. Every day is different. You’ll follow a personalized plan from your BCBA, implement behavior strategies, collect data, and build the consistent relationships that help kids grow. Your BCBA is closely involved and reachable, so there’s no guessing and no flying solo. What’s in it for you:$20–$27/hour, based on experience and locationDirect mentorship from a dedicated BCBA, not managers or a corporate chain of commandFull-time or part-time (some flexibility across mornings, afternoons, and evenings is needed to meet client needs; not sure if a schedule fits? Just ask, we have many)Career growth support, including a path toward BCBA certificationDepending on the practice: training reimbursement and paid hands-on learning for those earning their certification You’re a good fit if you:Genuinely enjoy working with children, especially kids who need extra patience and creativityHave an active RBT certification, or the drive to earn oneHave reliable availability across mornings, afternoons, or evenings, since our clients count on consistencyCome from education, childcare, psychology, social work, or any role where you showed up for kidsHave reliable transportation to reach client homes and schoolsCan keep up physically, getting on the floor, moving around, staying active (able to lift ~50 lbs)Are at least 18, have a high school diploma or equivalent, and can pass a background check Why Alpaca HealthWe’re not a big clinic chain. We’re a network of independent therapists who chose this work because they believe in it, and we match every RBT with a BCBA who mentors, not manages. We match families with providers who have availability now, and we work where families actually are. If you want a career where you see the results of your work every single day, this is it. Ready? Apply now.Not sure if you qualify? Apply anyway and tell us about yourself. We’d rather talk to one more curious person than miss someone great.

As a diverse by design school, we are committed to being inclusive and centering anti-bias/anti-racist education. We provide all students with an educational environment where learner variability is acknowledged, valued and supported. We view this variability as an inherent strength of our community and use it to inform classroom practices and lesson design. We also establish a strong sense of community where students reflect on their identities, learn from each other, develop critical reading and thinking skills, and are equipped with strategies to take action on issues they care about. The Behavioral Health Clinician- Professional will also provide education and advocacy to individuals and family members as directed by individualized treatment. This position is a supportive member of the interdisciplinary team. SPECIFIC DUTIES: 1. Performs initial intake and assessment/evaluation through the process of individual interview, interview of significant others and review of previous records, if available, for the purpose of gathering pertinent information to complete the assessment. 2. Develops a Treatment Plan to address specific identified needs which may include, but are not limited to: psycho/social (interpersonal) skills, self-esteem, depression/suicidal ideation, symptom control, anxiety and independent living skills. 3. Provides social work and other specialty interventions through individual, joint or group counseling. 4. Documents each individual session and writes progress notes based on each individual contact. Notes are to include progress toward long- and short-term goals, changes in Treatment Plan and other significant events. 5. Performs case management services for individuals who are found to need case management intervention. These services shall include, but are not limited to, treatment and community referrals, advocacy, psycho-education and crisis intervention. 6. Performs periodic evaluations to establish patient needs and determines how identified needs can be met. 7. Acts as liaison with other agencies and departments mutually involved in the individual’s care. 8. Completes discharge paperwork within regulatory requirements. 9. Serves as an advocate for family members, legal/forensic support, and outreach and engagement efforts. Must be well organized, demonstrate the ability to manage time effectively and demonstrate ability to maintain accurate records. jobs.description: Employer: NADAP, Inc. Expires: 09/24/2026 Join NADAP’s exciting new Pathways for Access to Careers and Employment (PACE) program in Brooklyn helping New Yorkers build their employment skills and careers! In this role, you’ll deliver hands-on career guidance, skills training, credential support, and job placement services all while making a real difference in your community. If you’re passionate about workforce development and ready to grow professionally in a mission-driven environment, PACE is where your impact and career take off!Position SummaryThe Career Coach is responsible for identifying, assessing, and preparing participants for employment opportunities through individualized career coaching, recruitment support, and workforce development services. jobs.title: Youth Program Teacher at City of Cambridge, MA
jobs.description: Employer: City of Cambridge, MA Expires: 09/24/2026 POSITION SUMMARY:The Youth Program Teacher leads a diverse cohort of preteen and middle school participants ages 9 to 13 in the Youth Center’s licensed afterschool program. Reporting to the Youth Center Director, the position provides direct supervision, mentorship, and support to youth and families throughout their engagement with the Youth Centers. The Youth Program Teacher develops and facilitates curriculum, programmed activities, service projects, civic engagement, leadership development, team building, and behavior management strategies that align with Cambridge Youth Programs values. The position balances administrative responsibilities, including attendance tracking and schedule coordination, with direct youth engagement, regular check-ins, team meetings, and program-wide activities, workshops, and field trips that support youth growth in a safe, engaging, and empowering environment. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES:The essential functions or duties listed below are intended only as illustrations of the various type of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.Manage cohort activities and behaviors during center activities inside and outside the building by supervising assigned spaces, actively monitoring youth, maintaining required staff-to-youth ratios, conducting headcounts during transitions, and ensuring the safe, orderly use of equipment and facilities.Provide direct supervision, mentorship, and support to assigned youth participants, including regular check-ins, cohort meetings, and activities that promote leadership, communication, teamwork, and positive youth development.Support Youth Workers and Group Leaders by providing necessary materials, information, and guidance and by assisting with planning, facilitating, and implementing workshops.Assist the Program Director in implementing youth-related policies and procedures, and support the Youth Center Director in program planning, day-to-day operations, and smooth program flow.Inform the Program Director of specific Youth Center member needs or concerns brought to your attention.Plan, design, organize, and implement age-appropriate programs and activities for preteens ages 9 to 13 within the assigned cohort and across the program; develop inclusive lesson plans aligned with curriculum, licensing requirements, and goals; integrate social-emotional learning, civic engagement, service, and leadership development; and plan and facilitate educational workshops with program staff.Plan and facilitate community meetings, team meetings, and group activities focused on Cambridge Youth Programs values, center expectations, youth leadership, and future planning.Provide a safe, structured, and engaging environment for Youth Center members and volunteers.Serve as a positive role model and build meaningful relationships with Youth Center members.Foster a positive group culture and sense of community within the assigned cohort and broader Youth Center program.Maintain open, friendly, and ongoing communication with families and schools regarding participants’ progress.Track attendance, coordinate schedules, and complete related administrative tasks to support daily program operations.Assist with organizing and participating in program-wide activities, workshops, field trips, and special events.Attend and fully participate in staff meetings, planning sessions, other meetings, and staff development and training programs and activities as directed.Perform related duties as required.Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions.QUALIFICATIONS:Education/ExperienceHigh school diploma or equivalent required; some postsecondary education preferred.Two (2) years of experience working with youth in academic, recreational, athletic, youth development, or related settings.Familiarity with Cambridge neighborhoods preferred.Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) and Sex Offender Registry Information (SORI) background checks required.An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:Knowledge of positive youth development, restorative practices, and age-appropriate programming for preteen and middle school youth.Skill in group management, facilitation, conflict resolution, and de-escalation.Skill in communicating effectively with youth, families, staff, schools, and other adults.Ability to create, plan, and implement curriculum, activities, workshops, and service or leadership development projects.Ability and interest in engaging and supporting families.Ability to support safe, inclusive, and structured program environments.Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.SUPERVISION RECEIVED:Works under the general direction of the Youth Center Director, with functional guidance from the Youth Center Director, exercising independent judgment in carrying out assigned program responsibilities within established policies and procedures. Work is reviewed through conferences, observations, periodic performance evaluations, quality of youth engagement, and compliance with program expectations and safety procedures. SUPERVISION EXERCISED:This position has no formal supervisory responsibilities, but provides day-to-day guidance and oversight to program participants and may provide functional direction to assigned volunteers or interns during program activities.WORK ENVIRONMENT:Work is performed primarily in a busy Youth Center environment, including classroom-style spaces, open activity areas, gymnasiums, and other program spaces. The position involves frequent interaction with youth, families, program staff, volunteers, interns, and community partners. Noise levels range from moderate to very loud depending on program activities, and work requires ongoing attention to youth safety, group dynamics, behavior support, and program flow. PHYSICAL DEMANDS:Work is active and program-based, requiring frequent standing, walking, movement throughout program spaces, and participation in youth activities. The position requires the ability to supervise youth in active settings, respond quickly during play or emergency situations, communicate effectively with youth and staff, and maintain visual and auditory awareness of program participants and surroundings. The position may require occasional running, bending, reaching, lifting, carrying, or moving program materials and equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions.REQUIRED DOCUMENTS:Please upload the following documents to complete your application:ResumeCover Letter The City of Cambridge's workforce, like the community it serves, is diverse. Applicants must have the ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups with a variety of identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies

jobs.description: Employer: Adoption Rhode Island Expires: 09/24/2026 Adoption Rhode Island is seeking a part-time, fee-for-service Clinician to join our Behavioral Health & Wellness team as an independent contractor. This flexible role offers up to 12 hours per week and provides permanency-competent, trauma-informed individual, family, and group counseling to children, youth, young adults, and families connected to foster care, adoption, and other child welfare experiences.The ideal candidate will value flexibility, bring strong clinical judgment and adoption-related experience, and be comfortable working independently while remaining connected to a collaborative team. Adoption Rhode Island is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to equity, inclusion, and respectful care for the children, youth, young adults, families, and communities we serve. Duties and ResponsibilitiesCarry active caseload, providing permanency-competent, trauma-informed individual, family and group counseling in an office setting, utilizing evidence-based and evidence-informed service models.Assist in the ongoing development and implementation of program service delivery, including supportive activities for legacy foster and adoptive young adults that provide hope, normalcy, and an opportunity to connect with other Adoption Rhode Island and community-based offerings.Maintain up-to-date documentation/client records, including but not limited to releases and authorization forms, assessments, treatment plans, progress notes, discharge summaries, and external reports. Actively participate in regularly scheduled individual supervision. Actively participate in monthly Behavioral Health & Wellness Team meetings. Attend agency staff meetings, and other agency forums, when available.Maintain client confidentiality and conduct self in accordance with professional and ethical standards.Assist the agency in assessing and providing effective, equitable, understandable, and respectful quality care and services that are responsive to diverse cultural beliefs and practices, preferred languages, mental and behavioral health literacy, and other communication needs.Promote coordination and collaboration of service delivery, both internally across agency programs and departments, as well as externally, with community partners and contractors. Contribute to and participate in agency community outreach activities, as well as additional support programming, as assigned. Education and ExperienceMaster’s degree in a mental health discipline requiredLicensure, with corresponding liability coverage requiredAt least five years of professional experience in the mental health, child welfare, or human services fields required Trauma-informed and permanency competence Other RequirementsMust pass Background Criminal Investigation (BCI) check Must pass Child Protection Services (CPS) background checks for RI as well as any additional states, per Adam Walsh Act of 2006.Compliance with I-9 verificationAbility to work a flexible schedule, including some evenings and weekendsAccess to reliable transportation Specific to staff-owned vehicles, staff must demonstrate:-Possession of valid driver’s license-Maintenance of clean driving record-Possession of valid and continuous auto insurance coverage that meets the state’s minimum requirements-Valid vehicle inspection sticker Hold an active license with the RI Department of health (RIDOH) Additional requirements, as outlined by service contracts, if applicablePhysical RequirementsProlonged periods of (1) sitting at a desk/meeting table and (2) working on a computer.Ability to self-transport to client and agency-related meetings and work within the RI communityU.S. Bureau of Labor and Statistics Occupational Requirements Survey (ORS) of strength level category: Sedentary to Light workReasonable accommodations may be made to enable staff to perform the essential duties.

jobs.description: Employer: The New York City Urban Debate League Expires: 09/24/2026 Our Commitment to YouThe NYCUDL is firmly committed to equal employment opportunity for all in all phases of employment, including the application process. We know that applying for a new job can be a daunting process. But we encourage all candidates with interest in joining our organization to apply. You may be just the person we need. If you have any questions about your application or the interview process, please email us at jobs@debate.nyc.NYCUDL MissionThe New York City Urban Debate League (“NYCUDL”) unlock the transformative power of debate for New York City public school students to develop the next generation of informed, compassionate, and courageous leaders.NYCUDL DescriptionThe New York City Urban Debate League is a nonprofit organization dedicated to expanding access to competitive debate across New York City, with a focus on teaching underserved students. To advance this mission, the NYCUDL provides comprehensive support for students, educators, and schools—including year-round instructional coaching for educators, student workshops, over 35 annual debate tournaments, four weeks of Summer Debate Institute, and the development of original curriculum, including more than 100 lesson plans for educators each year. The League has experienced significant growth in recent years. Since the 2018–2019 school year, student participation has grown by nearly 80%, from 2,260 to just over 4,000 students annually. The number of participating schools increased by 60%, from 160 to 250, and the number of Title I schools served nearly doubled. With active partnerships in all five boroughs, the NYCUDL is proud to be the largest urban debate league in the country and remains deeply committed to teaching debate, fostering student voice, and supporting academic confidence and civic leadership across New York City.Position OverviewCoordinator, Programming: Curriculum, Professional Learning & Dream Team assists with the administration of NYCUDL curriculum, professional learning programs, NYCUDL Summer Debate Camp, and any other special events. This role serves as the key administrative support for debate curriculum preparation, including topic research, slide and lesson plan creation for coaches. They will also lead the organization’s Dream Team, a group of students who travel to national tournaments and perform other duties as assigned. The Coordinator will report directly to the Manager, Programming: Curriculum, Professional Learning & Dream Team.Key ResponsibilitiesDevelop and maintain Public Forum and Parliamentary debate curriculum, under the supervision of the Program Manager and Director, across Open League, Districts, and NYC Reads, ensuring materials are appropriately scaffolded for each program’s format and student experience level.Partner with coaches and program staff to adapt lesson plans, drills, and case materials to the distinct needs of Open League, Districts, and NYC Reads, incorporating current topics and tournament trends.Train and support coaches on curriculum rollout across all three programs, gathering feedback from the field to continuously refine PF and Parli content.Lead NYCUDL’s Dream Team program (approx. 15% of role), coordinating travel, tournament preparation, and coaching for the select group of students competing at national tournaments. Plan and run Forensics Fridays, weekly workshops offering direct instruction that allows students to dive deeper into current topics alongside NYCUDL staff.Coordinate professional development opportunities within Forensics Fridays, connecting students with outside experts across relevant fields to enrich topic-specific learning.Qualifications & RequirementsEducation: Bachelor’s degree required Experience: Strong experience in speech and debate programsTechnical Skills: Some awareness of tournament software (Tabroom.com), cloud software (Google Workspace, Office 365), and AV presentation tools.Work Week: Employees are expected to work in-person, 5 days a week (a majority of Mondays & Fridays are remote in practice), including Saturdays when needed (not more than 2 per month throughout the school year). The expected work week is 40-50 hours. Comp time is offered for a full day of weekend work, with some stipulations..Work WeekEmployees are expected to work in-person, 5 days a week (a majority of Mondays & Fridays are remote in practice). This role involves Saturday tournament administration (approximately 2 per month during the school year) and evening events. Comp time is offered for weekend tournaments.CompensationSalary: $68,500 Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no employee contribution for individual plansCommuter Bonus: Monthly subway pass (OMNY/MetroCard) providedTime Off: 21 days of total annual leave (10 vacation, 5 sick, 5 personal, and your birthday), plus major holidays and additional wellness benefits The NYCUDL is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in its employment decisions, in accordance with state and federal law. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Projected start on September 17.

jobs.description: Employer: Oswego County Expires: 09/24/2026 Oswego County Social Services’ Mental Hygiene division has an immediate opening for a Mental Hygiene Law Program Specialist to coordinate, monitor, and support the Division’s Assisted Outpatient Treatment (AOT) program and related activities. The position serves as the Division’s subject-matter expert regarding AOT requirements and designated areas of New York State Mental Hygiene Law and provides technical guidance to staff, service providers, referral sources, and other stakeholders. jobs.title: Community Mental Health Specialist at Art of Recovery Service NFP (AOR)
jobs.description: Employer: Art of Recovery Service NFP (AOR) Expires: 09/24/2026 Community Mental Health Specialist/Assertive Community Treatment SpecialistReports to: ACT Team LeadDepartment: OutreachLocation: Libertyville At AOR, we believe that recovery is a personal journey, one that looks different for each individual. It’s not always straightforward, and it’s not always easy, but it’s always worth it. Our mission is to offer compassionate mental health services that empower people to take ownership of their recovery. We’re dedicated to supporting clients in reaching their full potential while creating a community that values resilience, mental wellness, and inclusivity. As a Community Mental Health/Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) Specialist, you will be a key part of this mission, working directly with clients to help them meet their mental health goals in a collaborative and supportive environment. You’ll provide 75% of care in natural settings—like clients’ homes and communities—where you’ll assess safety, offer guidance, and ensure that clients are receiving the support they need. Your role will involve responding to crises and health evaluations, making decisive interventions when necessary, and maintaining a focus on recovery and harm reduction. Additionally, you will help remove barriers to care by transporting clients in your personal vehicle to essential destinations such as medical appointments, food pantries, court appearances, and other services that support their recovery and well-being. In addition to client-facing work, you will also be responsible for managing a caseload, documenting services, coordinating care with other team members, and participating in on-call crisis support when needed. You will be expected to bring a trauma-informed, strengths-based approach to your work, working closely with clients who may be dealing with mental illness and co-occurring substance use disorders. Every day, you’ll be helping clients navigate their recovery journeys, ensuring that they receive the highest quality care, while embracing AOR’s mission of person-centered support and community integration. What You’ll Be Doing:Client Support: Conduct well-being assessments and check in with clients in their homes, communities, or via telehealth. Help them set and reach personal goals.Documentation: Complete service notes and required assessments like IM+CANS and LOCUS in our client management system.Collaborate & Adjust Goals: Regularly check in with clients and their support systems (family, providers) to make sure treatment goals are aligned and adjust as needed.Psychoeducation & Medication Support: Provide training on medications and monitor progress, working closely with our ACT RN Specialist for accuracy.Daily Life Skills: Help clients improve their independent living and daily life skills (e.g., managing finances, cooking, and personal hygiene).Support with Case Management: Assist clients in applying for entitlements like SSI/SSDI, Medicaid, and SNAP, etc.Transportation Support: Assist clients with transportation using your own vehicle, when needed.Model Best Practices: Use client-centered, recovery-focused, trauma-informed, and harm-reduction methods to guide your work.Team Communication: Stay connected with your team, sharing updates and collaborating on client care.Crisis Support: Provide on-call and telephonic crisis support as part of a rotating schedule.Coordinating Care: Work with other professionals (doctors, therapists, family) to ensure the best support for your clients. What We’re Looking For:Qualifications:Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Psychology, or a similar field (LPHA or QMHP certified), or a Bachelor’s degree in Human Behavioral Science (with coursework in social work, psychology, or counseling).Experience: 0-2 years working with individuals diagnosed with mental illness. We welcome candidates with a strong passion for learning and making a difference!License & Transportation: Valid Illinois driver’s license, access to a reliable vehicle, and car insurance (liability of $100,000/$300,000). Why Work With Us?Make a Real Impact: Support clients in their journey to recovery and be a part of their success stories.Great Team: Collaborate with a supportive, dedicated team of professionals who share your passion for client care.Career Growth: We offer ongoing training to help you develop your skills and grow in the field of mental health.Work-Life Balance: Enjoy a flexible schedule and a supportive environment, ensuring you have the tools to succeed.Competitive Pay & Benefits: Receive a competitive salary, healthcare benefits, and other perks. Job Type: Full-timeSchedule Options: Tues-Sat 8:00-4:30 Benefits:Dental insuranceHealth insuranceLife insuranceMileage reimbursementPaid time offParental leaveReferral programVision insurance Work Location: In person

Candidates who successfully complete the interview process may receive an internship offer. Internship assignments are finalized in February based on candidate interests, strengths, and business needs.Intern Relocation Assistance:Polaris provides relocation support for eligible interns working 35+ miles from their assigned location. jobs.title: AVID Tutor at Boise School District
jobs.description: Employer: Boise School District Expires: 09/24/2026 The AVID tutor position is part-time (up to 19 hours per week) and currently pays $16.65 per hour. To be an AVID tutor, you will need to be available for a few hours each week during the school day (Monday-Friday, 7:30am-3:15pm). AVID tutors do not work any nights or weekends and college students are scheduled around their college class times. If hired, you will be assigned to a junior high and/or high school within the Boise School District where you will facilitate tutorials in person. Please note that any offer of employment is contingent on authorization to work in the United States and a background check. Training is provided.We are currently looking for availability during the following time windows: Monday–Thursday, 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. You do not need to be available every day—please indicate the days and times that work for you within these windows.To give you more background on this exciting job opportunity, you should know that AVID is a college prep course that enrolls students that have the individual determination to work hard and be successful in rigorous coursework. They learn strategies that will help them on the road to college and in life. Our AVID Elective classes run tutorials with the help of tutors. Tutorials provide the opportunity for students to present questions they're confused about to a group of their peers. Their group members then help them figure out their point of confusion through inquiry based questioning. As an AVID tutor, your role is more of a "facilitator" than that of a tutor. You'll facilitate a group of about 7 students and encourage them to ask questions to the presenter to get them to think about the answer. AVID Tutoring is not what you typically think of when you’re thinking of tutoring. You don't teach as an AVID tutor, instead you encourage students to discuss, question and collaborate within their group.

jobs.description: Employer: University of San Francisco Expires: 09/24/2026 International Student Advisor University of San Francisco R0011653 USF Hilltop Campus Job Title:International Student Advisor Job Summary:GENERAL SCOPE OF POSITION:Reporting to the Assistant Director of International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS), the International Student Advisor performs duties in the two primary functional areas of immigration reporting and international student advising. The first functional area involves responsibility for reviewing and processing immigration document requests from international students and exchange visitors and assisting with federally-mandated compliance requirements related to the Student and Exchange Visitor Immigration System (SEVIS). The second functional area includes advising students, faculty and staff on immigration regulations and reporting requirements. This will also include resiliency efforts to retain our international student population.The International Student Advisor also assists with University retention programs and services through efforts that foster a sense of belonging and community for international students and exchange visitors. ISSS supports approximately 1500 international students and exchange visitors each year. Full Job Description: ACCOUNTABILITY: As part of the larger USF Community, the International Student Advisor collaborates and cooperates with other staff and across divisions and departments to create a supportive University community that encourages and supports student learning and development by: • Manifesting the mission, vision and values of the University • Advancing the division's mission and commitments • Embracing the strategic priorities of the division and University • Engaging differences in a manner that allows students with diverse perspectives, experiences and traditions to thrive within the University community • Providing experiences that challenge students to develop spiritually, intellectually, emotionally, physically, socially, culturally, and morally in order to prepare them to contribute to the University community and to the world • Drawing out the leadership qualities inherent in every individual, and to providing opportunities for students to apply knowledge and skills • Creating an environment that supports a socially responsible way of being together in community • Recognizing and celebrating the achievements and contributions of all students DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: • Serves as a Designated School Official (DSO) for the university's F-1 student program and as an Alternate Responsible Officer (ARO) for the university's J-1 exchange visitor program. (Must be a U.S. citizen or Permanent Resident as required by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and the U.S. Department of State). • Enters and maintains accurate student and exchange visitor data and generates SEVIS events using information systems including, but not limited to, Banner, the Terra Dotta database system and SEVIS batch file processing software, and the SEVIS Real Time Interface (RTI). • Provides support for the university's compliance with federal regulations governing students and exchange visitors, including required updates to students' and exchange visitors' SEVIS records. • In collaboration with ISSS staff, advise students and exchange visitors in a variety of matters including U.S. immigration regulations, cultural adjustment, personal matters, financial concerns, and university procedures. • Analyzes and interprets data for the timely and accurate processing of SEVIS events and production of immigration documents for students and exchange visitors • Collaborates with offices and departments (e.g., Admission, Registrar, International Admission, academic departments, CASA, AEM, etc.) to provide an integrated experience that helps international students and exchange visitors navigate campus processes and the U.S. culture. • In concert with the other ISSS staff, assist and/or lead the development, delivery and assessment of orientations, programs, and events for international students and exchange visitors, including International Student Orientation, International Education Week, and employment-related / tax workshops. • Provides support and advocate for international students by working with student clubs and organizations, and through outreach to determine student needs. • In collaboration with the other ISSS staff, assists with retention programs and services through efforts that provide a welcoming and supportive environment for international students. • Participates in the development and implementation of office policy and procedures. • Participates in the creation and ongoing revisions of electronic materials and resources. • Serves as a liaison with other campus units on specific projects and initiatives as assigned. • Assists with answering telephones and client reception as needed. • Other duties as assigned. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: • Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution is required. • Interest in working within the context of a diverse, Catholic and Jesuit University located in an urban, multicultural area. • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to investigate, assemble, analyze, interpret, and apply information from a wide variety of sources, such as the Code of Federal jobs.description: Employer: Aspire Public Schools Expires: 09/24/2026 ABOUT ASPIRE Aspire Public Schools operates a network of high-performing, college preparatory charter schools serving TK-12 scholars in communities across California. Founded in 1998—in an effort to transform the inequitable racial, social, and gender outcomes that our communities persist through—Aspire is one of the largest and most forward-thinking open-enrollment public charter school systems in the nation. Our purpose is to prepare our scholars for success in college, career, and life. At Aspire, we set a foundation for our scholars to gain knowledge, skills, and power to access and make choices for their families and post-secondary lives. Every day, our community of students, families, teachers and staff comes together to learn, work, and play in an environment grounded in our values of Bienestar (Well-Being), Culture of Belonging, Community Partnership, Agency & Self-Determination, and Joy. JOB SUMMARY The Speech-Language Pathologist carries out the speech and language instruction within a student’s individualized educational program for Aspire Public Schools. The Speech and Language pathologist instructs students with Individualized Education Plans in an inclusive environment. This role works closely with school sites, Special Education staff, and Aspire staff on a regular basis and may work with outside consultants and district personnel as needed. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS Provide direct, individual and/or small group instruction to identified students on a regularly scheduled basis as required in the IEP Regularly collaborates with team members, parents and related service providers for the purposes of: reviewing student data, ensuring IEP implementation, co-planning and/or co-teaching Participate in developing, implementing, and monitoring Individual Educational Plans for students who qualify for Related Services pursuant to California educational codes. Implement health and mobility supports (i.e. provide 1:1 support to student in classroom, support student/s with toileting needs, assist with health-related needs (g-tube, feeding, administration of medication) (under supervision of school nurse) and assist with the physical needs of students (lifting/ assisting with mobility, implementing student stretching/exercise routines.) Input weekly IEP service tracking and meet all IEP timelines Create and maintain notifications, records, files, and reports as required by federal, state, and SELPA regulations Develop a thorough progress monitoring tool for students, that is regularly shared with staff and parents and used for team decision-making. Communicate on a frequent basis with parents of students around student progress, and collaborate to gain parent input Collaborate with outside providers as needed and appropriate, with parent consent Provide oversight and support to SLPAs Additional: Demonstrate knowledge of, and support, the Aspire Public Schools mission, vision, value statements including antiracism, policies and procedures, operating instructions, confidentiality standards, and the code of ethical behavior. Knowledge of special education principles, concepts, methodologies, and documentation requirements Knowledge of special education assessment, planning, instruction, and evaluation Knowledge of child cognitive development and different learning styles Ability and willingness to implement students’ IEPs Belief in inclusion and Aspire’s Equity Belief Statements and demonstrates high expectations for students with diverse learning needs Ability and willingness to reflect and improve Ability to follow and meet mandated deadlines and due dates Flexibility and ability to adapt to changing conditions; ability and good judgment to take initiative to modify activities Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to collaborate with general education and special education colleagues, parents and community Ability to excel as a member of a team and implement new learnings from professional development Ability to work with an ethnically and economically diverse student body Perform other related duties as required and assigned. Competencies: Knowledge of speech and language assessment, planning, instruction, and evaluation Knowledge of child cognitive development and different learning styles Ability and willingness to implement students’ IEPs Belief in inclusion and Aspire’s Equity Belief Statements and demonstrates high expectations for students with diverse learning needs Ability and willingness to reflect and improve Flexibility and ability to adapt to changing conditions; ability and good judgment to take initiative to modify activities Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to collaborate with general education and special education colleagues, parents and community Ability to excel as a member of a team and implement new learnings from professional development Ability to work with an ethnically and economically diverse student body Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment; flexible, able to work autonomously as well as take direction as needed Ability to learn quickly and to be effective in a fast-paced, dynamic, entrepreneurial environment: able to work autonomously and thoroughly with independent self-reflection, as well as take direction as needed Alignment to and urgency around Aspire’s mission, vision and values Please click on the link below to apply on our company's website:https://jobs.jobvite.com/aspirepublicschools/job/oOHOufwx

jobs.description: Employer: Edmonds College - Faculty & Staff Recruitment Expires: 09/24/2026 Dean School of English Language Studies (ELI) SALARY: $122,226.59 - $126,843.76 LOCATION: Lynnwood, WA DESCRIPTION: The Dean for the International Education Division provides leadership, management, planning, oversight and advocacy for faculty, staff, and programs with a goal of ensuring student success within the International Education Division. The following departments and programs are currently included in the International Ed. Division: Academic English (AENGL), Communication/International Studies (COMM/INSTD), English Language Acquisition (ELA), ELA Student Services, Hotel and Tourism ESL (HTESL/Trajal), and the Intensive ESL department (INTEN). This is an exempt position reporting to the Vice President of Instruction. Applications received by September 24th, 2026, at 11:59 PM PST will receive priority consideration. Applications submitted after this deadline may not be reviewed unless a second round of review is deemed necessary. Position is opened until filled. RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:Assume primary responsibility for the recruitment, screening, orientation and continued professional development of full- and part-time faculty and staff within the division. This includes the management of the tenure process for probationary faculty in the instructional division.Supervise and support staff in Academic English, Communication/International Studies , English Language Acquisition (ELA), ELA Student Services, Hotel and Tourism ESL, and the Intensive ESL department including advisors, faculty and admin staff. Conduct evaluations of full- and part-time faculty and staff.Provide leadership in the development of effective teaching and learning strategies, as well as outcomes assessment tools.Ensure compliance with state and federal Basic Education for Adults (BEdA) standards and reporting requirements. Co-represent Edmonds College on the State Board’s Council for Basic Skills.Be responsible for student retention and success within the division.Establish and maintain identified FTES targets, monitor class enrollments, student-faculty ratios, and faculty loads, and work with department chairs to adjust class schedules and offerings as needed.Chair/Lead and/or participate in college-wide initiatives, committees and meetings.Develop and manage division budgets (state, self-support, and contract -funded areas); provide oversight for grant and contract development, implementation and compliance.Supervise the work of establishing/maintaining clear pathways and advising to College for English language learners. Partner with the Office of International Programs to offer appropriate and relevant course modalities, content, and pathway options that meet the demands of the international education market and the demands of both college F-1 visa holders and English language learner F-1 visa holders. DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:Demonstrated proficiency in budget and/or grant management.Demonstrated interpersonal skills and collaborative leadership style.Independent and self-motivated working style. PHYSICAL WORK ENVIRONMENT:Work is typically performed in an office setting, and onsite/in-person. The ability to sit at a desk/computer station, bend, stoop, walk and generally move around the office to consult with others, work within a busy environment and remain focused on tasks. The ability to speak clearly on the telephone, use a computer is required. Recurring early/late hours (weekend/early morning/evening meetings). Some tasks require lifting and moving of objects up to 30lbs. This position requires the ability to drive and use of a personal vehicle. The ability to make sound judgments is essential. WORK SCHEDULE:Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m., including some evenings and weekends. COMPENSATION: Salary is $122,226.59 - $126,843.76 and is based on the Edmonds College administrative/exempt salary schedule, plus a full state benefits package, which includes tuition waivers for college classes, medical, dental, retirement options and more. Vacation and leave package includes 12 sick days per year, 11 scheduled holidays, 1 personal holiday, and 24 vacation leave days per year. FLSA Status:The position is an exempt position under the Fair Labor Standards Act requirements. CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT:You must document your citizenship or employment authorization within three days of hire.Criminal background check. Prior to a new hire, a background check including criminal history will be conducted. Information from the background check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining the applicant’s suitability and competence to perform in the position.All new positions are contingent upon funding.At this time, Edmonds College does not sponsor H1-B Visas.Complete, sign, and submit Declaration Regarding Sexual Misconduct APPLICATION PROCEDURES AND REQUIRED DOCUMENTS:All applicants must apply online. No paper submissions or emailed materials will be accepted. Your online application must include the following documents in order to be complete: Current resume. Cover Letter addressing your qualifications and interestNames and contact information for three references.For veterans’ preference, please scan and attach your DD214, Member-4 Form. Important, if this position is posted on an external website other than www.edmonds.edu/hr or Edmonds College Job Opportunities page, please apply using one of those official links. Applications submitted through external websites will not be received in the College’s application system. ABOUT THE COLLEGE:Established in 1967, Edmonds College is a public community and technical college serving south Snohomish County. The college is guided by a mission centered on Teaching, Learning, and Community, with a strong commitment to academic excellence, student success, and community engagement. It serves about 18,000 students annually, including more than 800 international students from more than 55 countries. The college offers nearly 66 associate degrees and 111 professional certificates in 30 programs of study. Its highest enrolled programs are the Associate of Arts/Associate of Science degrees, Paralegal, Allied Health (pre-nursing degree), Business/Accounting, Construction Management, and Culinary Arts. The college is located in the center of the growing south Snohomish County communities of Edmonds, Lynnwood, Mountlake Terrace, Brier, Mill Creek, Mukilteo, and Woodway. For more information, visit www.edmonds.edu. EEO/AFFIRMATIVE ACTION STATEMENT:The college provides equal opportunity in education and in employment per state and federal law. For questions about our nondiscrimination policy or gender equality and athletic teams, contact Kathy Smith (Title IX and Section 504 Coordinator/Investigator); Clearview Building, Room 122B; kathy.smith@edmonds.edu, 425.640.1814.
